description: The provided image is a donut chart visualizing the distribution of two ambiguity-related metrics — “Ambiguity Std (Outer)” and “Max Ambiguity (Inner)” — likely from an analysis in the paper “Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs.” The chart consists of two concentric rings: the outer ring represents “Ambiguity Std” with four categories (Std: 0.0, Std: 0.47, Std: 0.82, and an unlabeled gray segment), while the inner ring represents “Max Ambiguity” with three categories (Max: 1, Max: 2, Max: 3). The outer ring’s segments are labeled with percentages: 49.0%, 47.7%, 7.0%, and 5.0%, though the legend does not explicitly map these percentages to the Std values. The inner ring’s segments are labeled 38.0%, 39.0%, and 14.2%, corresponding to Max: 1, Max: 2, and Max: 3, respectively. The color scheme uses varying shades of blue for both rings, with darker tones for higher Std values and lighter tones for higher Max values. The chart appears designed to show how ambiguity (both in standard deviation and maximum value) is distributed across different categories, potentially reflecting model behavior or attack success rates under varying ambiguity conditions.
